title: Microsoft Purview Audit: what the unified audit log records, how long it keeps it and what it costs
summary: The documented controls, licensing requirements and retention limits are supported by Microsoft Learn. The page correctly reports the conflicting Microsoft guidance about AI auditing charges and Dataverse retention rather than presenting either interpretation as settled.

claims.claim: In the Microsoft Purview portal, Audit > Start recording user and admin activity enables auditing.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. If the Audit solution card isn't displayed, select View all solutions and then select Audit from the Core section. ... Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true turns on unified audit logging.
claims.quote:
Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing.
Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal provides audit search at Audit > Search.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog supports -StartDate, -EndDate, -UserIds, -Operations and -ResultSize for audit searches.
claims.quote:
Search-UnifiedAuditLog
    -EndDate <ExDateTime>
    -StartDate <ExDateTime>
    [-Operations <String[]>]
    [-ResultSize <Int32>]
    [-UserIds <String[]>]

claims.claim: Audit > Search in the Microsoft Purview portal is the UI audit-search surface alongside programmatic search.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/security/auditLog/queries creates an audit search query through Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote:
Create a new auditLogQuery object.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/auditLog/queries

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal provides Audit > Create audit retention policy.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... Select Create audit retention policy, and then complete the following fields on the flyout page

claims.claim: New-UnifiedAuditLogRetentionPolicy uses -Name, -RecordTypes, -RetentionDuration and -Priority to create a retention policy.
claims.quote: New-UnifiedAuditLogRetentionPolicy -Name "Microsoft Teams Audit Policy" -Description "One year retention policy for all Microsoft Teams activities" -RecordTypes MicrosoftTeams -RetentionDuration TenYears -Priority 100

claims.claim: Dataverse auditing is reached in Power Platform admin center through Security > Compliance > Auditing > environment > Set up auditing > Turn on auditing.
claims.quote: From the left-side menu, select Security > Compliance. ... Select the Auditing tile. ... Select the environment ... Select Set up auditing. In the Auditing pane, select Turn on auditing.

claims.claim: The displayed GET organizations query retrieves auditsettings, isauditenabled, auditretentionperiodv2, isuseraccessauditenabled and useraccessauditinginterval using Dataverse Web API v9.2.
claims.quote:
GET [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations?$select=
auditsettings,
isauditenabled,
auditretentionperiodv2,
isuseraccessauditenabled,
useraccessauditinginterval HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: The start-recording banner is displayed when auditing is off.
claims.quote: If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity.

claims.claim: Turning auditing off is documented through PowerShell.
claims.quote: Use Exchange Online PowerShell to turn off auditing.

claims.claim: Searching audit records requires the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits: Admin units
claims.claim: A restricted administrator can search and export only user-generated audit logs within their assigned administrative units.
claims.quote: A restricted admin can only search and export user-generated audit logs within the scope of their assigned administrative units.

claims.claim: The Graph audit-search operation requires an AuditLogsQuery permission, with AuditLogsQuery.Read.All an available permission.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | AuditLogsQuery-Entra.Read.All | AuditLogsQuery-CRM.Read.All, AuditLogsQuery-Endpoint.Read.All, AuditLogsQuery-Exchange.Read.All, AuditLogsQuery-OneDrive.Read.All, AuditLogsQuery-SharePoint.Read.All, AuditLogsQuery.Read.All

claims.claim: Retention policy cmdlets run in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can also use Security & Compliance PowerShell to create and manage audit log retention policies.

claims.claim: Creating audit retention policies requires the Organization Configuration role.
claims.quote: You need the Organization Configuration role in the Microsoft Purview portal to create or modify an audit retention policy.

claims.claim: An organization can have up to 50 audit log retention policies.
claims.quote: Your organization can have up to 50 audit log retention policies.

claims.claim: The default Audit Premium retention policy cannot be modified.
claims.quote: Audit (Premium) in Microsoft Purview provides a default audit log retention policy for all organizations. You can't modify this policy.

claims.claim: Changing Dataverse audit configuration requires System Administrator, System Customizer or equivalent permissions.
claims.quote: You must have a system administrator or system customizer role or equivalent permissions to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Anyone can view Dataverse audit configuration.
claims.quote: Anyone can view the configuration, but you must have the System Administrator or System Customizer role to change the settings.

claims.where: controls[4].note; What it is: Dataverse auditing
claims.claim: Dataverse audit configuration has separate environment, table and column settings.
claims.quote: You can configure auditing at three levels: environment, table, and column. First, turn on auditing at the environment level. To log data changes in a table, turn on auditing for the table and for the column.

claims.where: controls[4].note; What it is; Cost and licensing: Dataverse
claims.claim: Dataverse audit logs consume Dataverse log storage capacity.
claims.quote: Dataverse stores audit logs and they consume log storage capacity.

claims.claim: The Dataverse REST call shown in the inspection row is read-only.
claims.quote:
Retrieve organization settings
Use the following queries to retrieve your organization settings.
GET [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations?$select=

claims.where: summary; What it is: first paragraph
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Audit records user and administrator operations across Microsoft services in the searchable unified audit log.
claims.quote: Your organization's unified audit log captures, records, and retains thousands of user and admin operations performed in dozens of Microsoft services and solutions.

claims.claim: Each audited activity produces an audit record.
claims.quote: When a user or admin performs an audited activity, the system generates an audit record and stores it in the audit log for your organization.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What it is: first paragraph
claims.claim: The unified audit configuration and search cmdlets shown are used in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog. ... You have to run this cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview provides Audit Standard and Audit Premium tiers.
claims.quote: The following table compares the key capabilities available in Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium). Audit (Premium) includes all Audit (Standard) functionality.

claims.claim: Audit Standard is enabled by default for organizations with the appropriate subscription, subject to the SMB and unmanaged-trial exceptions described later.
claims.quote: Audit (Standard) is enabled by default for all organizations with the appropriate subscription.

claims.claim: Audit Standard retains current audit records for 180 days.
claims.quote: In Audit (Standard), the system retains records for 180 days, which means you can search for activities that occurred within the past six months.

claims.claim: Audit Premium adds audit log retention policies.
claims.quote: Audit (Premium) builds on the capabilities of Audit (Standard) by providing audit log retention policies

claims.claim: Audit Premium supports retention up to one year without the long-term retention add-on.
claims.quote: Create customized audit log retention policies to retain audit records for longer periods, up to one year (and up to 10 years for users with the required add-on license).

claims.where: What it is; Cost and licensing: 10-year retention
claims.claim: Retention up to 10 years requires the per-user 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on in addition to Audit Premium licensing.
claims.quote: In addition to the required licensing for Audit (Premium) ... a user must be assigned a 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on license to retain their audit records for 10 years.

claims.claim: Audit Premium adds intelligent insights.
claims.quote: Audit (Premium) builds on the capabilities of Audit (Standard) by providing ... high-value intelligent insights

claims.claim: Audit Premium provides higher Office 365 Management Activity API bandwidth.
claims.quote: Audit (Premium) includes higher bandwidth access to the Office 365 Management Activity API, which provides faster access to audit data.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and agent records
claims.claim: Copilot interactions are logged automatically as part of Audit Standard when organization auditing is enabled.
claims.quote: The system automatically logs these activities as part of Audit (Standard). If your organization enables auditing, you don't need to take extra steps to configure auditing support for Copilot and AI applications.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and agent records
claims.claim: Cowork interactions generate audit logs automatically.
claims.quote: The system automatically generates audit logs when a user interacts with Copilot, Cowork, or an AI application.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and agent records
claims.claim: AI application interactions are supported by automatic audit logging, with the pay-as-you-go enablement qualification described in Cost and licensing.
claims.quote: The system automatically generates audit logs when a user interacts with Copilot, Cowork, or an AI application.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and agent records

claims.claim: Copilot audit records have an AppHost property identifying the host application.

claims.claim: Dataverse auditing records changes to records within a Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: Dataverse auditing logs changes that you make to customer records in an environment with a Dataverse database.

claims.claim: Dataverse auditing also records user access.
claims.quote: Dataverse auditing also logs user access through an app or through the SDK in an environment.

claims.claim: Dataverse audit logs are stored in Dataverse rather than being the unified audit log itself.
claims.quote: Dataverse stores audit logs and they consume log storage capacity. ... User access or activity logging is sent to Purview for production environments only.

claims.claim: Dataverse user access and activity logging are sent to Purview only for production environments.
claims.quote: User access or activity logging is sent to Purview for production environments only.

claims.claim: The Dataverse activity-logging option is visible only when minimum Microsoft Office licensing requirements are met.
claims.quote: The option to turn on activity logging is only visible when the minimum MicrosoftOffice licensing requirements are met.

claims.where: Why it matters: first paragraph; Risks and limits: Retention
claims.claim: Audit retention depends on the license of the user who performed the activity, allowing 180-day or one-year retention.
claims.quote: The length of time that an audit record is retained (and searchable in the audit log) depends on your Office 365 or Microsoft 365 Enterprise subscription, and specifically the type of the license that is assigned to specific users.

claims.where: Why it matters: second paragraph; Risks and limits: Logging
claims.claim: Auditing is not enabled by default for Business Basic, Business Standard and Business Premium SMB licenses.
claims.quote: Auditing isn't enabled by default for Small and Medium Business (SMB) licenses, including Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Business Standard, and Business Premium.

claims.where: Why it matters: second paragraph; Risks and limits: Logging
claims.claim: Unmanaged tenants using enterprise license trials must enable auditing manually.
claims.quote: Unmanaged tenants that use free trials of enterprise licenses don't have auditing enabled by default. In both these cases, you must manually enable auditing for your organization.

claims.claim: Purview audit searches return no results when auditing is turned off.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing, searches of the audit log in Microsoft Purview return no results.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog returns no results when auditing is turned off.
claims.quote: Running the Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell also returns no results.

claims.claim: The Office 365 Management Activity API cannot access organization audit data when auditing is turned off.
claims.quote: If you turn off auditing in Microsoft 365, you can't use the Office 365 Management Activity API or Microsoft Sentinel to access auditing data or logs for your organization.

claims.claim: Microsoft Sentinel cannot access organization audit data when auditing is turned off.
claims.quote: If you turn off auditing in Microsoft 365, you can't use the Office 365 Management Activity API or Microsoft Sentinel to access auditing data or logs for your organization.

claims.claim: Audit Standard and Premium require an appropriate organization subscription.
claims.quote: Licensing for Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium) requires the appropriate organization subscription that provides access to the audit log search tool

claims.claim: Logging and retaining audit records also has per-user licensing requirements, with plans linked from Microsoft's subscription requirements.
claims.quote: and per-user licensing that's required to log and retain audit records. ... For a list of subscription and licensing requirements for these auditing solutions, see the subscription requirements for Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium).

claims.where: Cost and licensing: One year retention
claims.claim: For one-year retention, the activity-generating user needs Office 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft Purview Suite or an E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on.
claims.quote: To retain an audit log for longer than 180 days (and up to 1 year), the user who generates the audit log ... must have an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license or a Microsoft Purview Suite ... or E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Non-Microsoft AI applications
claims.claim: Audit logs for non-Microsoft AI application interactions use pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Audit logs for non-Microsoft AI applications use pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Non-Microsoft AI applications
claims.claim: The pay-as-you-go audit meter is the number of audit records processed.
claims.quote: Audit solutions | Audit logs for user interactions with non-Microsoft generative AI applications | Number of audit records processed

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Non-Microsoft AI applications
claims.claim: Non-Microsoft AI interaction audit logs are retained for 180 days after pay-as-you-go enablement.
claims.quote: You need to enable pay-as-you-go features to turn on these logs. When you enable them, the system retains these audit logs for 180 days.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Non-Microsoft AI applications
claims.claim: Purview pay-as-you-go requires an associated Azure subscription.
claims.quote: The billing mechanisms are Azure based, so you must associate your Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.

claims.claim: The Copilot audit page says Security Copilot is included in Audit Standard rather than pay-as-you-go auditing.
claims.quote: Pay-as-you-go billing doesn't apply to Microsoft applications. All Microsoft applications, including Microsoft Copilots like Microsoft Security Copilot

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Non-Microsoft AI applications

claims.quote: All Microsoft applications, including Microsoft Copilots like Microsoft Security Copilot, Copilot in Microsoft Fabric, and custom applications built using Microsoft Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry are included in Audit Standard.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Non-Microsoft AI applications; Open questions
claims.claim: The Copilot audit page says custom applications built using Copilot Studio are included in Audit Standard.
claims.quote: All Microsoft applications, including Microsoft Copilots like Microsoft Security Copilot, Copilot in Microsoft Fabric, and custom applications built using Microsoft Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry are included in Audit Standard.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Non-Microsoft AI applications; Open questions
claims.claim: The Get started page instead lists Fabric Copilot, Security Copilot and Copilot Studio among non-Microsoft 365 AI data requiring pay-as-you-go auditing.
claims.quote: you must enable pay-as-you-go billing for your organization. This data type includes Copilot in Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Security Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Studio, and any connected or cloud AI application.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Non-Microsoft AI applications; Open questions
claims.claim: The Copilot audit page names the audit-record consumption unit but does not state a per-record rate.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview Audit Copilot audit records per record rate pricing audit-copilot; site:learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-copilot "rate" "price". Read audit-copilot in full and purview-billing-models; audit-copilot gives no numeric rate.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Logging; What to check: first bullet
claims.claim: Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled in Exchange Online PowerShell verifies auditing, with True indicating it is on.
claims.quote:
Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled
A value of True for the UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled property indicates that auditing is turned on.

claims.claim: Get-AdminAuditLogConfig in Security & Compliance PowerShell always reports False for UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled.
claims.quote: Although the Get-AdminAuditLogConfig cmdlet is also available in Security & Compliance PowerShell, the UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled property is always False, even when auditing is turned on.

claims.claim: Audit records for non-E5 users are retained for 180 days.
claims.quote: If you have non-E5 users or guest users in your organization, their corresponding audit records are retained for 180 days.

claims.claim: Audit records for guest users are retained for 180 days.
claims.quote: If you have non-E5 users or guest users in your organization, their corresponding audit records are retained for 180 days.

claims.claim: A 10-year audit retention policy is not retroactive.
claims.quote: This policy isn't retroactive and can't retain audit logs that were generated before the 10-year audit log retention policy was created.

claims.claim: Audit records generated by service principals, system events and application activities are retained for one year.
claims.quote: Audit records generated by non-user entities (such as service principal actions, system events, and application activities) are retained for a fixed period of one year.

claims.claim: The one-year retention of non-user audit records is not configurable.
claims.quote: This retention period isn't configurable and custom audit log retention policies don't apply to these records.

claims.claim: Custom audit retention policies do not apply to non-user audit records.
claims.quote: This retention period isn't configurable and custom audit log retention policies don't apply to these records.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Records are not instant
claims.claim: Core-service audit records typically become available 60 to 90 minutes after an event.
claims.quote: For core services (such as Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams), audit record availability is typically 60 to 90 minutes after an event occurs.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Records are not instant
claims.claim: Microsoft does not commit to a specific audit-record availability time.
claims.quote: Microsoft doesn't guarantee a specific time after an event occurs for the corresponding audit record to be returned in the results of an audit log search.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Records are not instant
claims.claim: Broad search jobs in large tenants can take up to 48 hours.
claims.quote: In large tenants with a high number of users, broadly-scoped Search jobs may take up to 48 hours to complete.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Search has ceilings
claims.claim: The portal audit-search date range is limited to 180 days.
claims.quote: The maximum date range that you can specify is 180 days. An error is displayed if the selected date range is greater than 180 days.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Search has ceilings
claims.claim: Each administrator account can run up to 10 audit search jobs concurrently.
claims.quote: Each admin Audit account user can have up to 10 search jobs running at the same time, with a limit of one unfiltered search job.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Search has ceilings
claims.claim: Only one of an administrator's concurrent search jobs can be unfiltered.
claims.quote: Each admin Audit account user can have up to 10 search jobs running at the same time, with a limit of one unfiltered search job.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Search has ceilings
claims.claim: Audit Standard portal search-result export supports up to 50,000 rows.
claims.quote: Export supports results up to 50,000 rows for Audit (Standard) and up to 1,000,000 rows for Audit (Premium).

claims.where: Risks and limits: Search has ceilings
claims.claim: Audit Premium portal search-result export supports up to 1,000,000 rows.
claims.quote: Export supports results up to 50,000 rows for Audit (Standard) and up to 1,000,000 rows for Audit (Premium).

claims.claim: Unrestricted administrators can access non-user and system-account audit logs.
claims.quote: An unrestricted admin has access to all audit logs, including logs generated by non-user and system accounts.

claims.claim: Dataverse auditing does not audit retrieve operations.
claims.quote: Furthermore, auditing doesn't support retrieve operations or export operations.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Dataverse auditing has gaps
claims.claim: Dataverse auditing does not audit export operations.
claims.quote: Furthermore, auditing doesn't support retrieve operations or export operations.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Dataverse auditing has gaps
claims.claim: Dataverse auditing does not support table or column definition changes.
claims.quote: Auditing isn't supported on table or column definition changes or during authentication.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Dataverse auditing has gaps
claims.claim: Dataverse auditing does not support authentication auditing.
claims.quote: Auditing isn't supported on table or column definition changes or during authentication.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Dataverse auditing has gaps
claims.claim: Separate Dataverse activity logging, called Read logs, covers retrieval and export.
claims.quote: In addition to Dataverse auditing, you can turn on Dataverse and model-driven apps activity logging to log data retrieve operations and export operations. ... activity logging (Read logs)

claims.claim: Dataverse audit records are stamped with the retention period active when written.
claims.quote: Each audit log is stamped with the currently active retention period.

claims.claim: The Dataverse admin guide says changing the retention period does not change existing records, while the page explicitly acknowledges conflicting guidance.
claims.quote: Changing the retention period here doesn't change the retention period for already existing records. The new retention period applies to all new records created after the retention policy change.

claims.claim: The same Dataverse admin guide also says the Security page auditing option can apply retention to existing logs.
claims.quote: Use the Security page auditing option to set the retention policy. This option provides the flexibility to apply the retention policy to existing logs.

claims.claim: The developer configuration reference says ApplyRetentionToExistingLogs is ignored.
claims.quote: ApplyRetentionToExistingLogs | Apply new retention policy to existing audit records. | No, is ignored.

claims.claim: Audit Reader and Audit Manager have the audit-search roles by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Microsoft Purview portal Role groups page assigns these roles to the Audit Reader and Audit Manager role groups.

claims.claim: Access to audit cmdlets requires the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in Exchange admin center.
claims.quote: Use the existing Audit Logs and View-Only Audit Logs roles in Exchange admin center to grant access to audit cmdlets.

claims.claim: Custom audit retention policies override the default policy.
